text: {"score":4,"justification":"The summary is accurate and well grounded. The headline (7 of 10, 70%) matches the card. The rationale figures match too: 30.8% vs 4.3% expected, risk-adjusted score 21.24, z 4.01, 32% low-complexity share, 38 documented claims, and 4 of 29 with no lab on the claim. The cited claims check out. C0076627, C0076995 and C0077120 are in the below-billed examples, and C0077120 is also a low-complexity claim with 1 condition (hyperlipidemia, age 32). C0076565, C0076824 and C0076832 are low-complexity 99215 claims with the stated ages and conditions. The language is cautious (\"reason to review, not a finding\"), and the next steps are concrete. The weaknesses are minor. Only 10 documented 99215 claims is a thin base, and the summary does not flag that. The 10% comparison figure is not on the card (the card shows 9.8%, so it is a rounding). The three low-complexity examples show no documentation, so they support only the complexity point. The next steps do not tell the investigator to request records for claims not yet documented. Nothing says the 1.6% documented share is small, or that records may not be representative. The \"0 or 1 chronic conditions\" phrasing for the 32% share is fine. The 5 example claims do not include a high-complexity or supported 99215 for balance.","problems":["Thin documentation base (10 documented 99215 claims, 1.6% of claims documented) is not flagged as a limitation","Three of the six cited claims are low-complexity examples with no documentation, so they support only the complexity point, not the below-billed finding","No balancing mention of the 3 documented 99215 claims that were supported, or the high-complexity 99215s","The comparison rate \"10%\" is a rounding of 9.8% and is not explained","The summary does not say that the 4 of 29 no-lab figure is a weak signal, since a lab may not be needed for data review","Next steps are somewhat generic and do not specify which undocumented claims to request"]}
